outcome.technical: R3: manage-worktrees.py task-add now adopts a tree already marked for the task (adopt_task_tree) instead of refusing 'already has a tree' - the lookup runs before the non-empty-path check; the marker records setup 'pending' until run_setup returns and then its status (provision()), and an adopted tree whose marker does not record a completed setup (ran/none) gets the include and setup again; adoption reports the marker's base. drive-phase.py add_tree records a per-task base (wave.bases) from the verb's answer, no longer records a tree whose setup failed (so the next step re-asks task-add, which adopts it and re-runs setup before dispatch, no attempt spent), and pops keptTrees on adoption; close_wave carries every still-standing tree into state.keptTrees and names a blocked member's tree with its path; retire_member names the kept tree's path. R1: audit-lookup.py wave_tree() returns (tree, base) with the per-task base; the task-mode reviewer brief gets a Tree section and its diff is read as git -C <tree> diff <base> (untracked from the tree too). R4: wt8 discard-then-close case plus wt8m twin. Tests: test_drive_phase stages wt-block (wt1-wt4), wt5-block (wt5-wt6), wt7-block (wt7, wt8, wt8m); test_manage_worktrees ta8 rewritten to the adoption contract, ta8a and su5a added.
